reconcile.note: Fausset reads Chronicles' 35 cubits as the two pillars' combined length, each being about 17½, rounded to 18 in Kings.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats Chronicles' multitude of numerical discrepancies with Samuel-Kings as a general feature of the book, of which this pillar height is one instance.

quotes.text: the problem still really was, as before, how to explain the complete difference of general conception and the multitude of discrepancies in details
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the multitude of discrepancies between Chronicles and the older historical books.

sides.verseText: For he fashioned the two pillars of brass, eighteen cubits high apiece: and a line of twelve cubits compassed either of them about.

sides.snippet: two pillars of thirty-five cubits high
sides.verseText: Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty-five cubits high, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five cubits.
